The Lever That Made the Model Work

让模型动起来的杠杆 · 645 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1An engineering institute invited pupils to build a working model for an exhibition. Its theme was an invention that could make a daily task easier. An inventor named Zed had designed a small device to raise a heavy lid. The inventor's first model used electronic controls and a motor. A visitor with limited grip could press the switch, but the machine stopped halfway. The sponsor wanted a more advanced controller. Zed asked the pupils to look at the mechanism before they changed its technology.

2They drew a diagram from mechanics. The lid rotated around a hinge. A gear moved it, but friction increased where the parts touched. A physics student marked the arm and measured its dynamics with a phone camera. A mathematical model related force and distance. The calculation was a guide to an experimental change. It could not show how much an aging spring would drag until they tested it under load.

3One pupil proposed more automation. Another suggested new electronics and a magnetic catch. Zed wanted a lever made from spare hardware first. He asked a student from an architecture course to construct a frame. Its base flexed during the first trial. A rigid block beside the joint improved stability. An industrial apparatus could use a more complex mechanism. Their prototype needed a change they could understand and reproduce without a major investment.

4The lever lifted the lid, but a chip received a signal too early. An internal sensor showed the exact point. A programmer reviewed the controller and added a short delay to separate a genuine stop from a brief vibration. A technician checked that the modification left the emergency release functional. His persistence had exposed a fault in the first test. That technological refinement followed the mechanical one. It would be misleading to credit a more advanced processor for the change in the lever's position.

5They invited visitors with various needs. One could reach the button but not see the light. Another preferred a manual handle. The team installed both and used a camera for motion detection. They compared completion time, effort, and practicality under each condition. Efficiency meant less strain on the user, not simply more features. An instructor suggested integrating both choices into one design and keeping an accessible way to open the lid without electricity.

6A physicist asked how the device would work on a robot and whether it would have to adapt to different loads. A pupil drew a robotic hand that could grip the lever, then noticed the extra joint it would need. The team compared the motion with a simple algebra exercise. No new silicon chip could make the hinge sit in the right place. The contrast helped a younger visitor see which parts of the invention could evolve, and which depended on the same basic principle.

7A judge asked whether a manufacturer could adopt the design. A pioneer in robotics had worked on the same problem. The group made a methodical test of a cheaper material. It wore quickly. They wrote an industrial maintenance note and explained which part could be replaced. A patent or a sale would not be their first measure of success. They wanted an owner to understand the construction and a technician to service the device with ordinary tools. That outcome made the model worth presenting to another class.

8A visitor asked what the pupils had managed to invent. Zed let her manipulate the lever by hand, then try the switch. She admired the practical change in effort. A tech company might want to commercialize the controller, but the pupils used a simpler test. Could a visitor explain the new capability to someone else? She traced the hinge and showed her friend how it worked. That clear communication gave the group a way to share its design concept. A mechanical oddity had become a clear experiment for another class.

四级汇总词汇 · 45中文译文

让模型动起来的杠杆

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1一所工程学院邀请学生为展览做一个能实际运行的模型，主题是发明怎样让日常任务变简单。发明者泽德做了一台抬起重盖子的小装置。第一个模型用电机和电子控制。一位抓握不太有力的参观者能按开关，可机器抬到一半就停住了。赞助方想换更先进的控制器。泽德请学生先看看机械结构，再决定要换什么技术。

2他们按力学原理画了示意图。盖子绕铰链转动，由齿轮带动，可零件接触处的摩擦变大了。一个学物理的学生在力臂上做了标记，用手机摄像头测它怎样运动。他们用数学模型表示力和距离的关系。计算能给试验改动指个方向。至于老化的弹簧带载时会拖慢多少，还是得实际测。

3一个学生主张提高自动化，另一个建议换电子元件，再加磁扣。泽德想先拿备用零件做个杠杆。他请学建筑的学生搭支架。第一次试验时，底座发生弯曲。关节旁加了块硬质垫块，支架就稳多了。工业设备可以用更复杂的装置。这台原型先要改出一个大家都能理解、也能照着做的方案，花不了一大笔钱。

4杠杆抬起了盖子，但芯片太早收到了信号。内置传感器指明了具体位置。程序员检查控制器，加了一点延时，让系统能分清真的停住和短暂的抖动。一位技术人员确认，改动后紧急释放装置仍然有效。他坚持检查，才在第一次试验里找出那个故障。技术上的改进跟在机械改动之后。杠杆位置变好，主要还是机械结构改对了。

5他们请不同需求的人来试。一位够得着按钮，却看不见指示灯。另一位更喜欢用手柄。团队把两种方式都装上，用摄像头检测动作，比较每种条件下所用的时间、力气和实际操作的便利。所谓提高效率，是让使用者更省力。指导老师建议，把两种选择都放在同一设计里，并留一个断电时也容易打开盖子的办法。

6一位物理学家问，要是把装置用到机器人身上，它能不能适应不同重量。一个学生画了一只可以握住杠杆的机械手，随即发现还得多一个关节。团队把这段运动和一道简单的代数题作了比较。换硅芯片也不会让铰链自己挪到正确位置。这个对照让一位年纪更小的参观者看清，发明的哪些地方可以继续变，哪些仍取决于同一个基本原理。

7评委问，制造商能不能采用这个设计。机器人领域的一位先行者也做过同样的研究。学生有条理地测了一种更便宜的材料，发现它磨损很快。他们写了一份工业维护说明，交代哪个部件可以更换。大家首先看重的是，使用者能否看懂结构，维修人员能否拿普通工具维护它。做到这两点，模型就值得拿给另一个班看。专利或销售可以以后再谈。

8一位参观者问，学生究竟发明了什么。泽德请她先用手扳杠杆，再试试开关。她亲自感到了少用多少力。科技公司或许会想把控制器做成商品，但学生用的检验方法很简单。她能把新增的功能讲给另一个人听吗？她沿铰链比画，给朋友讲清了工作原理。讲得明白，团队就能把设计想法分享出去。一个古怪的机械装置，就这样变成了另一个班也能看懂的实验。
